features.title: Root timed questions keep the Agent working
features.summary: With the web seed's tool-ask-user row in mode: timed, a root Agent's ask_user_question shows a counting-down card; when the foreground wait ends the Agent gets a pending result and keeps working, a later answer arrives as a user message tagged answer_to_pending_question, and stopping the turn withdraws the form.
failureModes: The timed schema exists only where the profile selects it: the web seed's preset-standard row sets tool-ask-user mode: timed, and a profile without that row gets the blocking legacy schema.
While the card is open it takes the composer's place, so Stop generating is reachable only after closing the panel ("reopen it from the tool call").

After a Host restart the pending card is shown again, but the root Session is stopped; delivering an answer to a stopped root Session is a Host gap (see plans/dsh-host-gaps.md), so the journey proves the card survives, not that a post-restart answer reaches the Agent.

externalDependencies.boundary: DSH's own timed ask_user_question tool and its userQuestions service; agent-questions only restyles its card and reads its projection.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: The loopback fake Command Code provider issues the ask_user_question call and records the pending tool result and the late reply.

features.title: Steady countdown and compact native question card
features.summary: Restyles the native async question card: a tabular, fixed-width countdown, a header that stacks under 480px, and a question clamped to three lines that expands on hover or focus.
failureModes: The rules key on the native card's data-question-key attribute, element structure and CSS-module class suffixes, so a DSH update that reshapes the card drops them silently.
Without DOM access there is no "Show more" button; the clamped question expands only on hover or keyboard focus inside the header.

telemetry.reason: Client-only: Steady countdown and compact native question card renders browser state and starts no Host work of its own.

features.title: List and answer thread questions
features.summary: Root Agents can list timed native questions across Sessions or by id, plus direct-child durable questions, with recommendation, timeout, and answerability metadata. Continued native forms and parent-scoped child questions use their authorized answer tools.
failureModes: A non-root Agent attempts cross-thread native access.
An open native form remains on the answerer waterfall or its target root is not live.
The Session projection is unavailable or a legacy-schema question has no timed projection.

verification.testName: lists pending questions by direct parent with exact deadline and child filter
records a timed deadline, continues after a pending result, then settles on reply
marks continued native forms answerable only for live root Sessions

features.title: Subagent questions in the Inbox, answerable in place
features.summary: Every pending, unexpired child-to-parent question is a blocking Inbox item about the parent thread, with the question options as answer choices. Choosing one answers as the parent thread (which must be running), wakes the waiting subagent, and resolves the item; a question answered, expired or cancelled elsewhere resolves by itself.

features.title: Thread questions in the Inbox
features.summary: Every native ask_user_question form waiting in a live root thread is a blocking Inbox item about that thread. A continued form with one single-select question is answerable in place with its options, through the same native answer API as answer_thread_question; any other form says to answer it in the thread. The item resolves when the form settles or its thread stops.
failureModes: Only forms the native question projection tracks are listed: it records forms whose tool schema is the timed one, so a legacy-schema form stays out of the inbox (the same coverage as list_thread_questions).
A form still open on the native answerer waterfall is refused in place and answered in its thread; the native answer API takes continued forms only.
Without the inbox (activity-timeline) loaded, questions work exactly as before; the provider reconciles when the inbox announces it is ready.
The native question fork (@dshfiles/user-questions) keeps its upstream no-op Host half; agent-questions already reads the forms Host-side, so it owns this provider.
